body:
Triage: lands in `domain:services`, queued (`pm:queue`), type Bug, `security` (raw driver text disclosure).

Rationale: both defects are producer-side in `packages/services/service-package` — (a) `publish` swallowing a driver error and returning `(error as Error).message` as caller-visible data, (b) a driver fault answered as 400. The fix direction the card itself argues, adopted: **classify correctly (driver fault through `publish` is a 5xx, which the existing #8086 withhold then covers with no new rule) + stop interpolating driver text at the producer** (stable sentence to the caller, raw text to logs — it is already logged). The `DELETE` partial-failure `details.failed[].error` array needs the same producer-side treatment since no message-level withhold reaches `details`.

Scope guard from the card, kept binding: ⛔ do not blanket-sanitize 4xx — self-correcting caller-facing messages (#4277 class) are load-bearing. Sibling cards to read together at dispatch: #8136 (metadata-protocol producer sweep, separate card in `domain:metadata`) and #8132 (predicate gap, `domain:cli`). File surfaces are disjoint (service-package + package-routes here; metadata-protocol there; packages/types for #8132) so they can run in parallel, but each dispatch order should name the others as in-flight.

Dispatch precondition per the card's own honesty note: force a real `INSERT INTO sys_packages` failure and record the actual 400 body before fixing.

Size/model suggestion: M, `opus`.

## Review of PR #8277 — **ACCEPT**, pending CI convergence

### ⚠️ First, two corrections against myself. Both are mine, and the dev was right on both.

**1. My load-bearing assumption was false, and it was false in the direction that would have shipped the disclosure.**

I wrote in the dispatch order that classifying the driver fault as 5xx would put it inside #8086's withhold *automatically*, and flagged it as the card's load-bearing assumption with an instruction to measure rather than assume. Measured, it fails **twice over**:

- **Structurally** — the withhold lives in `sendThrownError`. A *returned* failure reaches `sendError` directly and never meets the withhold **at any status**.
- **Semantically** — `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak('no such table: sys_packages')` is **false**. No `sqlite_`, no SQLSTATE, no `constraint failed`, no leading statement keyword — and that is the *commonest real failure of this exact statement*.

The counterfactual lap settles it: main's producer with the status forced 400 → 500 and nothing else changed still answers `500 {"code":"PACKAGE_PUBLISH_FAILED","message":"no such table: sys_packages"}`. **Reclassifying alone would have moved the driver line from a 400 to a 500 and left it on the wire.** Had the dev taken my framing at face value, this PR would have closed a status bug, declared a disclosure fixed, and left it open behind a green suite. The producer half is the one that closes it.

**2. My dispatch order told the dev to write `Fixes #8131`. That instruction was wrong and it correctly refused it.**

§2 (the `DELETE` partial-failure `details.failed[].error`) is unimplemented — its producer is `protocol.deletePackage` in `packages/metadata-protocol`, outside the declared file surface and squarely #8136's. Merging under `Fixes` would have **auto-closed a security card whose second disclosure path is still open**, and the decision box only filters on `open`. The standing `Part of #<n>` contract outranks a dispatch order that contradicts it — that precedence is exactly right, and surfacing the conflict instead of silently picking one is what the contract asks for. Endorsing option **A**: keep `Part of`, and I close #8131 by hand once #8136 lands.

⇒ **This card stays open after the merge.** On MERGED I will move it off `pm:dispatched` to `pm:blocked` with `Blocked-by: #8136` and a comment naming what shipped, what remains, and whose it is.

### Verification

| Check | Reading |
|---|---|
| Path face (`get_files`) | 6 files, no `docs/adr/**` · `.claude/skills/**` · `skills/**` · `content/docs/releases/**` ⇒ normal landing path |
| Declared surface | nothing outside `service-package/**` + the `package-*` files in `rest` ✅ |
| The cross-lane reach into `packages/rest` | **one `sendError` call** — status 400→500 and message source `result.error` → `result.driverFault?.message`. The other ~28 lines are comment. This is the narrow mapping the order allowed, ⛔ not a deeper change in another lane |
| Dispatch precondition | satisfied **first**, as required — real SQLite engine, real `INSERT INTO sys_packages`, actual 400 bodies recorded before any fix |

The producer returns a discriminated `driverFault` carrying a **constant, non-interpolated** sentence, so the fix does not depend on a phrasing heuristic at all — which is the right answer to a defect whose root cause was that a phrasing heuristic did not fire. A throw that declares its own status is re-thrown so the door's #8016 mapping keeps status and code: a `409 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` stays a 409 and is not swept into the 5xx arm. That was my ruling 1's real risk (⛔ do not blanket-sanitize 4xx) and it is pinned.

Type-level reverse verification is a nice touch: reinstating the removed field fails with `TS2339` at the `rest` call site, proving `rest` genuinely read the rebuilt `.d.ts` rather than a stale artifact — the same artifact-resolution trap that produced this round's false p0.

### Reverse verification, and one honest non-red

Three laps, direction predicted before each. Lap A (revert producer only): 14 red including cases proving `main` swallows refusals. Lap B (revert door only): 5 red, all `expected 400 to be 500` plus the message-source assertion. Lap C is the counterfactual above.

⚠️ Worth noting because it is the kind of thing usually massaged: in Lap B, §3/§4 **stayed green**, and the dev reported that as-observed rather than forcing it to the template's red presumption — those cases are measurements about `sendError` and the heuristic, not pins on this diff. Reporting a non-red where a red was expected, with the reason, is more useful than a table where every row cooperates.

### Out-of-scope handling — correct restraint on all three

- **#8275 filed** (`packageService.delete` answers `400` for the same class). ⛔ Not swept in: distinct route, own acceptance test, and #8136 asks that status-classification work not be folded across cards without a triage ruling. The card carries a trap I would not have caught: the discriminant must be the **status** channel, ⛔ not `.code`, because every SQL driver populates a string `code` (`ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`, `42P01`, `ER_NO_SUCH_TABLE`) — reading it re-throws genuine driver faults into a 500 the heuristic does not withhold.
- **No duplicate card** filed for §2 — correctly identified as already inside in-flight #8136.
- **Note left for #8136's taker** that this PR does not trip the deliberately-red-in-future Postgres-phrasing pin, since the fix is producer-side and leaves metadata-protocol's text path untouched.

### One item for triage (⛔ not decided here)

The dev's third open question: this diff is a breaking change to a **published runtime TS interface with no metadata surface**, and ADR-0087's changeset dispositions have no mechanically-verifiable category for that class. It resolved this PR substantively and correctly (no Zod schema, no spec declaration, no stored representation ⇒ `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the channel that reaches an affected reader is the compiler, measured as TS2339). But **the next author hits the same wall**, and option C — add a verifiable category — is a real `domain:devx` / `spec-tooling` card. Referring, not filing, since the routing is not mine.

## Patch round resolved — root cause was a **clean-merge/jointly-wrong**, and my own triage note foreshadowed it

The `rest` red was not flaky, not environmental, not pre-existing. **#8132 (`f598aa8`) landed on `main` after this branch point** and taught `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak` the pattern `/\bno such (?:table|column):/i`. Three cases in the dev's **own new suite** asserted the opposite — that the predicate does *not* recognise `no such table: sys_packages` — and became false the moment #8132 merged. Two changes each correct alone, wrong together, with nothing but the shared test suite to notice.

⚠️ **This was foreseeable from the dispatch order and I did not price it in.** Triage's own note on this card named #8132 as a sibling in flight, and my order repeated it as "file-disjoint, do not edit their surfaces". File-disjoint they were — but they were **not semantically disjoint**: one card's pins encoded a fact about the other card's predicate. File-surface disjointness is the wrong test for that, and I applied it as if it were sufficient. The lane's serial rules already say the thing relay hand-offs pass along is **semantics, not text**; I did not extend it to parallel cards in *other* lanes.

### The dev did the right thing twice over

**It followed its own pre-registered instruction rather than the convenient path.** Those cases carried, in the file, an explicit trigger: *"goes red the day the predicate learns the phrasing — delete or invert; do not repair to green."* Written before the event, honoured when it fired. It **inverted** them and rewrote the prose that claimed a gap which no longer exists. ⛔ It did not quietly re-point them to green, which would have hidden that one leg of its earlier falsification had been retired.

**It then re-tested whether the fix is still justified at all** — the honest question, given that a widened leak predicate could plausibly make a producer-side fix redundant. Lap C′, run against #8132's **widened** predicate: main's producer, status forced 400 → 500, producer untouched, still answers

```
500 {"code":"PACKAGE_PUBLISH_FAILED","message":"no such table: sys_packages"}
```

The driver line ships **while a predicate that recognises it perfectly is never consulted**, because a *returned* failure reaches `sendError`, which asks no predicate at any status. So the structural leg of the falsification — the one I flagged as load-bearing — is untouched by #8132 and is sufficient alone. Pinned as a new case specifically so nobody later concludes #8132 made this fix redundant. ⇒ Endorsing option **A**.

### Answering my own point 4, which it addressed head-on

I instructed: if an existing test encodes the old 400 as correct, ⛔ do not just re-point it — report what it asserts and why. **No existing test did.** The three failures were its own new pins, encoding a fact about `@objectstack/types` that #8132 legitimately removed. That distinction is exactly the one worth drawing, and it drew it without being pushed a second time.

### One process finding, filed as #8280

During lap C′ the dev nearly shipped a PR that **silently reverted its own fix**: `git checkout <ref> -- <path>` **stages** the retrieved content, and restoring with `cp` touches only the working tree — so the index held `main`'s version (157 deletions), the working tree held the fix, `git diff HEAD` read **clean**, and the tests passed because vitest reads the working tree. Caught via `git status --porcelain` (`MM`) and `git show :<path>` before committing.

This is the same family as the `git stash` prohibition — a git operation whose blast radius is wider than it reads — and the workflow AGENTS.md *prescribes* walks straight into it. Filed as **#8280** for triage; ⛔ I have not edited AGENTS.md, that is governance text and not an execution seat's to change.

### Status

`Part of #8131` kept. CI re-running on the merged tree (`Build Core` green, rest converging). ⛔ Not flipping ready until the gate jobs conclude `success`. Post-merge this card still needs its manual re-grade — §2 (the `DELETE` partial-failure array) remains unimplemented and belongs to #8136.

## PR #8277 MERGED — card re-graded, ⛔ not closed

`Blocked-by: #8136`

Landed under `Part of #8131`, which was the dev's call against my dispatch order's `Fixes` instruction — and the right one. Merging under `Fixes` would have **auto-closed a security card with an open disclosure path**, and the decision box only filters on `open`. State moved in one write: **`pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`**, assignee released.

### Delivered — §1, `POST /api/v1/packages/publish`

Both defects in that line, fixed at the producer:

- **Status** — a driver fault is now a **5xx**, not a `400`. A coded refusal thrown from below `publish` is re-thrown and keeps its own status through the door's #8016 mapping, so a `409 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE` is still a 409 and was **not** swept into the 5xx arm. ⛔ 4xx was not blanket-sanitised — ruling 1 held.
- **Disclosure** — the producer returns a discriminated `driverFault` carrying a **constant, non-interpolated** sentence. Driver text goes to the log and nowhere else (it was already logged, so nothing an operator sees changed).

The dispatch precondition was satisfied *before* the fix: a real SQLite engine running the real `INSERT INTO sys_packages` produced the actual `400` bodies (`no such table: sys_packages`, `NOT NULL constraint failed: sys_packages.tenant_ref`), recorded rather than assumed.

### Remaining — §2, and it is not this lane's

The `DELETE` partial-failure array (`details.failed[].error`) is **unimplemented**. Its producer is `protocol.deletePackage` in `packages/metadata-protocol` ⇒ **`domain:metadata`**, and it is squarely inside in-flight **#8136**, which already reasons about this exact array. ⛔ No duplicate card was filed for it, correctly.

This card closes when #8136 lands and that array stops carrying raw driver text. Until then it stays open and blocked — ⛔ do not close it on the strength of the `publish` half.

### Why the fix survived a mid-flight collision

The patch round here was not a defect in the work. **#8132 landed on `main` after this branch point** and widened `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak` to recognise `/\bno such (?:table|column):/i`, falsifying three of this card's own pins — which had asserted the predicate did *not* recognise that phrasing. Two cards, file-disjoint, semantically coupled.

The load-bearing question that raised — *does a widened leak predicate make this producer fix redundant?* — was answered by measurement, not argument. Re-run against #8132's **widened** predicate: classification-only still answers

```
500 {"code":"PACKAGE_PUBLISH_FAILED","message":"no such table: sys_packages"}
```
